_comment: Understood table layouts, emitted field by field by tools/disasm_all.py. Each table: bank, addr (hex CPU address), label (an alias; Data_BBB_AAAA labels are kept), count, id_base (optional; record index + id_base is shown in comments), id_names ("monster" appends the monster name to the id comment), fields (db N bytes | words N bytes shown as little-endian dw values | ptr = 16-bit pointer into the same bank, or into the bank given by the field bank_from indexes; "stream": true registers the target as a compressed stream),, optional record (a short description printed instead of the list of field names), and note. Every layout cites its evidence in docs/EVIDENCE_LOG.md. Field names state only what the evidence supports.

tables.label: ActionEffectTable
tables.note: E-0126 (C1: DispatchActionEffectTable (36:6717) jumps through the word at $6726 + 2 * wBattleActionId; E-0053 and E-0084 counted 240 entries ending at $6906, where the first effect routine starts).

tables.label: SkillTable

fields.name: first number the debug skill viewer shows; rises across a spell family (2, 4, 10 for Blaze, Blazemore, Blazemost)
skill family: string index in category $12 (1 = Blaze, 2 = Firebal, 3 = Bang, ...)
skill type: string index in category $13 ('Type A' ... 'Type G')
low 2 bits: when usable, string index in category $14 (0 None, 1 Battle, 2 Field, 3 Anytime); high nibble: string index in category $10 ('Charge', 'Mixed', 'Cautious', ...)

tables.note: E-0032 (C1: the debug mode's skill viewer, GameMode0 state 9, loads 17-byte records with LoadSkillRecord and prints these fields; the screens were read on the emulator; 175 records because the viewer wraps its index at $AF). The meaning of the numbers is not established beyond that the first byte rises across spell families (Blaze 2, Blazemore 4, Blazemost 10).

tables.label: MonsterTable

fields.name: picture number: index into MonsterPictureTable, MonsterAttributeMapTable and MonsterPaletteTable (at most $0179; ids 1, 2, 3 = Slime, SpotSlime, CactiBall use pictures 10, 2, 145)
byte 22: personality axis copied to save-record offset $6F (graded with weight 9 by PersonalityIndexOfRecord)
byte 23: personality axis copied to offset $70 (weight 1)
byte 24: copied to offset $71 (not used by PersonalityIndexOfRecord)
byte 25: personality axis copied to offset $72 (weight 3)

tables.note: E-0033 (C1: LoadMonsterRecord copies a 26-byte record from here by 16-bit id (wCFE6/wCFE7); ids at or above $250 use bank $A2 instead, so this table has 592 records; record 1 holds 25, 0, 10, 7, 8, 7 and then $C8 $C8 $64 $C8, exactly the values the opening monster's save record shows for its HP, MP, ATK, DEF, AGL, INT and next four bytes; the order of the six stat words is confirmed by the pause menu's INFO panel, E-0046). Skill ids stay below 175 (one record, id 88, has $C8 in the fourth slot). Bytes 22-25 equal the save record's bytes at offsets $6F-$72 for the opening monster (E-0034); the three used by PersonalityIndexOfRecord are the personality axes. The first word is the picture number (E-0041): drawing the pictures it names gave a slime for monster 1 ('Slime'), another slime for monster 2 ('SpotSlime') and a spiky ball for monster 3 ('CactiBall'); monster names are the strings of bank $88 (category = id >> 8, index = id & $FF).

tables.label: ItemTable

fields.name: 16-bit amount (10, 50, 500, 200, 2000 for the first five items)

tables.note: E-0034 (C1: LoadItemRecord copies 13 bytes from here by item id (wD081) to wD084; RunItemEffect dispatches on the same id; wC61D is a 24-slot bag of such ids, empty at the start of a new game, matching the item menu's 'No items'; the herb handler compares the words at save-record offsets $5B and $5D to refuse use at full HP). 99 records: the next bytes are a different table. The meaning of the fields is not established beyond the first amount being 10, 50, 500, 200 and 2000 for ids 1-5.

tables.label: MapTable

fields.name: map record in this bank, indexed by the map number hMapId
fields.reason: map record of the map table

tables.note: E-0036 (C1: the pointer for map 56 is the record whose tileset stream (57:6E96) the game decompressed to $9000 on the emulator while hMapId was 56; the table has 256 words and ends where the first record begins; entries 30, 31 and 39 are not valid pointers and the system strings for map numbers 30, 31 and 39 (index 10 + number) read 'NO'; map 29 is the ship deck where a new game starts and the string at index 39 is 'Deck'). Records are 48 or 66 bytes; the first three far pointers (address and bank byte) name streams: the tileset for $9000 and, in later fields, the tile map for $C198 and the attribute map for $D000.

fields.name: list of warps for this map number (hMapId); a list ends with $80; maps without warps share one empty list
fields.reason: warp list of the map warp table

tables.note: E-0036 (C1: CheckWarpAtPlayer indexes it with hMapId; the lists hold entries matched against the player's facing and position, and a match queues sound effect $60 and loads a new map number and position; all 256 words point into the bank; the first list starts at $69A6, directly after the table).

tables.label: ScriptCommandHandlers

fields.name: handler that runs one frame of script command type (index + 1)
fields.name_note: runs one frame of script command type

tables.note: E-0038 (C1: ExecuteScriptCommand indexes it with wScriptCommandType - 1; command types are set by the fetch handlers of FetchScriptCommand; a zero word is an unused type; all 248 words are code pointers inside the bank and the table ends where the next bytes stop being pointers).

tables.label: ScriptOpcodeHandlers

fields.name: fetch handler for this script byte (opcode)

tables.note: E-0039 (C1: the inline table after FetchScriptCommand's `rst $00`, indexed by the script byte; 249 words, 49 distinct handlers: opcodes 0-12 each have their own, and most others share ScriptFetchGeneric, which makes the opcode byte the command type and starts the command (the command then reads its own arguments from the script pointer); a zero word is an unused opcode).
